content_preview.title: Nuxt 4.6 Adds a nuxt/server Import Surface and Vue Vapor Mode Interop, Alongside a Rebuilt Nuxt CLI v4 With a 73% Smaller Install
content_preview.summary: Nuxt 4.6 ships a server-agnostic nuxt/server import surface, interop support for Vue 3.6 Vapor Mode and a root app secret, alongside Nuxt CLI v4.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Nuxt team released Nuxt 4.6 on October 5, according to the [Nuxt 4.6.0 release notes on GitHub](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/releases/tag/v4.6.0). The same notes say that "Alongside the release of Nuxt v4.6, today also brings a new major release of the Nuxt CLI: @nuxt/cli v4." The headline changes are a server-agnostic import surface called `nuxt/server`, interop support for Vue 3.6's Vapor Mode, and a built-in application secret for sessions.

All status 200, manifest suspicious_patterns null for all three (nothing to adjudicate). source-0: released 05 Oct 22:11 (datetime 2026-10-05T22:11:57Z); contains the 'Nuxt CLI v4' section quoted verbatim ('Alongside the release of Nuxt v4.6, today also brings a new major release of the Nuxt CLI: @nuxt/cli v4'); nuxt/server described as 'an import surface (nuxt/server) for the server utilities that will be needed by most apps', still 'powered by Nitro by default'; 'the same handler runs under Nitro v2, Nitro v3 or @nuxt/vite-server, and a module that imports from nuxt/server doesn't need a peer dependency on h3 or nitropack'; @nuxt/vite-server is flagged 'highly experimental and the API will change'; 'Nuxt now supports Vue 3.6's Vapor Mode in interop mode', root stays on virtual DOM, components opt in via the vapor attribute on <script setup>; runtimeConfig.appSecret / NUXT_APP_SECRET; sessions sealed into a cookie with iron, no server-side storage; typed fetch rebuilt on fetchdts with peak memory 946 MB to 140 MB; 'Most of what's new in Nuxt 5 is already in 4.6, either as the default or behind a flag'; 'npx nuxt upgrade --dedupe'; Upgrading note 'This release requires Node.js ^22.22.3 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0' (verbatim). source-1: released 05 Oct 18:22 (2026-10-05T18:22:23Z); 'more than 200 commits since v3.37'; table v3.37.0 to v4.0: @nuxt/cli install size 13.1 MB to 3.5 MB -73%, dependencies 70 to 31, nuxt dev first paint 330 ms to 50 ms, memory at rest (Linux) 630 MB to 440 MB; nuxt curl, nuxt task, nuxt docs and the interactive terminal UI with keyboard shortcuts all present. source-2: page labelled 'Pre-release', 'v3.6.0-rc.10', released 30 Sep 09:01 (2026-09-30T09:01:06Z). The Vue page has no body text beyond the changelog pointer, so it supports only the release-candidate status and date, not any Vapor claim; the Vapor interop claim rests on the Nuxt notes, as the article attributes it.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Scrutiny items: (1) 73% figure: the measured quantity is the installed size of the @nuxt/cli package, 13.1 MB (v3.37.0) to 3.5 MB (v4.0), shown as -73% in the Nuxt team's own table. The title says 'a Rebuilt Nuxt CLI v4 With a 73% Smaller Install', which is accurate; the baseline (v3.37) and metric are given in the body, and the body and 'What We Don't Know' section frame the figures as the Nuxt team's own measurements. The title itself carries no attribution or baseline, which is a normal headline compression and not a defect. (2) Vapor Mode: the article never calls Vue 3.6 or Vapor stable; it says 'Vue 3.6 itself is still in pre-release' and 'a release candidate', and uses 'interop mode' exactly as the Nuxt notes do (opt-in per component, app root stays on virtual DOM). (3) nuxt/server is named correctly and described faithfully. (4) The only Node minimum in the article is the Nuxt 4.6 release requirement, copied verbatim from the Upgrading note; no CLI-specific minimum is given. Note: the same Nuxt notes elsewhere state the CLI requirement as v22.21+, v24.11+ or v26+, so the source itself lists two different figures; the article does not conflate them and is accurate to the passage it cites. (5) Dates verified: Nuxt Oct 5, CLI Oct 5, Vue rc.10 Sep 30. All three snapshots contain the cited entry. (6) Nothing rests on nuxt.com. (7) What We Don't Know notes the figures are the Nuxt team's own and that no independent benchmarks were cited; it does not literally say 'no independent coverage', but conveys the equivalent. (8) github.com is allowlisted. Every body URL appears in article.sources; no orphan URLs. No direct quotes beyond the one verified verbatim above.
